items.stem: What is the main role of the ground segment in space mission operations?

options.text: To command the spacecraft and receive its telemetry and data
options.rationale: Correct: the ground segment commands the spacecraft and receives telemetry.

options.text: To physically repair the satellite in orbit
options.rationale: Routine in-orbit physical repair is not the ground segment's role.

options.text: To replace the need for any orbit
options.rationale: The ground segment supports, not replaces, the orbit.

options.text: To generate the spacecraft's electrical power
options.rationale: Power is generated onboard, not by the ground segment.

items.explanation: Correct: the ground segment commands the spacecraft and receives telemetry.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO statements about mission operations are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Telemetry lets operators monitor spacecraft health and status
options.rationale: Correct: telemetry conveys health and status data to the ground.

options.text: Contact windows limit when a ground station can talk to a satellite
options.rationale: Correct: visibility passes constrain communication times.

options.text: A satellite is always visible to every ground station
Operations stop the moment a satellite reaches orbit
options.rationale: Operations continue throughout the mission life.

items.explanation: Correct: telemetry conveys health and status data to the ground.

items.stem: Why does responsible mission operations include end-of-life disposal planning?

options.text: To reduce orbital debris and protect the space environment for others
options.rationale: Correct: disposal mitigates debris and preserves usable orbits.

options.text: Because satellites are legally required to explode
options.rationale: Disposal is about safe removal, not destruction by explosion.

options.text: Because debris poses no risk to anyone
options.rationale: Debris is a real collision risk to other spacecraft.

options.text: Because orbits are infinite and self-cleaning
options.rationale: Orbits are finite resources and debris persists.

items.explanation: Correct: disposal mitigates debris and preserves usable orbits.
